title: Annual Public Transport Subsidy Amount and How This Compares with Other Government Subsidies and Support
what_it_is: Annual Public Transport Subsidy Amount and How This Compares with Other Government Subsidies and Support

sections.label: Public transport expansion and subsidies
sections.summary: Commuters gained from rail and bus expansion, while Government subsidises public transport over $2 billion yearly and committed $60 billion to rail.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Commuters have benefited from a 40% expansion of the rail network, 80 new bus services, reduced peak-hour waiting times for basic bus services from 30 to 15 minutes, as well as significant improvements in rail reliability from 67,000 to over one million mean kilometres between failures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: From 2012 to 2021, operating costs for public transport increased by 7% per year on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Government, currently, subsidises public transport services by more than $2 billion a year, or about $1 for every journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In addition, we have committed over $60 billion to expand and renew the rail network over the next decade.

sections.label: Government public transport subsidies
sections.summary: Government subsidies of about $2 billion a year cover public transport, roughly $1 billion each for trains and buses.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And the slack, in general, has been picked up through Government subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And as I have said, today, the Government subsidy is of the order of the magnitude of $2 billion a year, about $1 billion each for our train and for our bus services.

sections.label: Public Transport Vouchers for households
sections.summary: About 600,000 Public Transport Vouchers were announced, benefiting up to 40% of Singapore households, with continued provision for vulnerable segments.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Members may recall that, last year, when the fares were increased, we also announced about 600,000 Public Transport Vouchers would be made available.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Or if you include those who have no income, it is up to the 40th percentile or the fourth decile, so, up to 40% of Singapore households would be able to benefit from those Public Transport Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And we will make sure that we continue to address the needs of these vulnerable segments through an appropriate provision of such Public Transport Vouchers.
